requirement.part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip

brief:
Part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip. Solid rectangular cross-section, width across the load, thickness in the load direction.
Load 600 N at the tip, length 150 mm.
REQ-001 yield margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.25 (MS = allowable / (factor x stress) - 1).
REQ-002 ultimate margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.4.
REQ-003 tip deflection <= 1.5 mm.
REQ-004 width 20-80 mm, thickness 3-8 mm.
REQ-005 thickness must be a stock plate thickness: [3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 30] mm.
REQ-006 REQ-001 to REQ-003 must still hold with the load 10% higher and the plate 0.5 mm thinner.
REQ-007 thickness / width <= 2 (a proxy for lateral stability).
Materials: {"Al 6061-T6": {"density_kg_m3": 2700, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 68.9, "yield_mpa": 276.0, "ultimate_mpa": 310.0}, "Ti-6Al-4V": {"density_kg_m3": 4430, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 113.8, "yield_mpa": 880.0, "ultimate_mpa": 950.0}, "Steel 4130": {"density_kg_m3": 7850, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 205.0, "yield_mpa": 435.0, "ultimate_mpa": 670.0}}
Goal: the lowest mass that meets every requirement.

reasoning: Need one note per material before specialists run physics checks. Quick sizing sense: cantilever tip load P=600 N, L=150 mm, rectangular b x t, bending about width axis with thickness t in load direction. Stress sigma = 6PL/(b t^2), deflection = 4PL^3/(E b t^3). Stress governs for the thin/narrow end; deflection with E=68.9 GPa for Al will be the binding constraint, so Al needs the largest section. Ti and steel have higher E-to-yield advantage in different ways: Ti has high yield (880) so stress is easy, but E=113.8 is low so deflection governs; steel has E=205 GPa, so deflection is easy, stress (435 MPa) governs. Stock thickness and t/b<=2 constrain thickness choices. Load +10% and thickness -0.5 mm check (REQ-006) must be applied to the final design.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Search widths 20-80 mm with thickness 5-8 mm; deflection (E=68.9 GPa) is the likely binding constraint, so favor thicker, wider sections and check REQ-003 first. Stress (276 MPa yield) is secondary but must still pass with the 1.25 factor and the +10% load case.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Stress is easy to meet (880 MPa yield), so search thinner sections, roughly 3-5 mm thick and 20-40 mm wide, where the low modulus (113.8 GPa) will make deflection the binding limit. Keep t/b <= 2 (REQ-007) and verify REQ-003 under the REQ-006 case.
notes.Steel 4130: Deflection is easy to meet (E=205 GPa), so stress (435 MPa yield) governs; search the lighter end of the envelope, roughly 3-6 mm thick and 20-40 mm wide, while watching the high density (7850 kg/m^3) for mass. Verify REQ-001 and REQ-002 with the 1.25 and 1.4 factors under the +10% load and -0.5 mm thickness case.

text: I'll start by checking three candidates spanning the range, including the widest and thickest corner, which should show whether deflection can pass at all.
I'll start with three candidates that bracket the feasible range: the widest and thickest allowed section, plus two smaller ones.
I'll start by checking three Steel 4130 candidates across different thicknesses. Deflection looks like it will govern for thick plates, so I'm including a few widths that should satisfy it.

The three results match my hand calculation, and the 80 × 8 mm section is the largest allowed section in the envelope. Before I finalize, I'll check whether any design inside the thickness limit can meet deflection, and what thickness is actually needed.

No Al 6061-T6 design can meet all requirements. Tip deflection is the binding constraint, and it cannot reach 1.5 mm anywhere inside the allowed envelope (width 20–80 mm, thickness 3–8 mm). Deflection falls with both width and thickness, so the 80 × 8 mm corner is the stiffest possible section, and it still gives 2.87 mm. Meeting 1.5 mm would need about 10 mm of thickness, which REQ-004 excludes.

Thickness is limited to 3–8 mm by REQ-004, which rules out my earlier thicker candidates (REQ-004 fails for 12 mm and 10 mm). Only the 8 mm plate remains viable, so I'll check whether width can drop below 69 mm and whether thinner plates can work at the 80 mm width limit.
The 68 mm width fails REQ-006 (deflection 1.515 mm under the worst case), so 69 mm is the minimum width at 8 mm. I'll verify two more widths so I have four checked proposals.

**No Ti-6Al-4V design inside the stated envelope meets all requirements.** The binding limit is tip deflection (REQ-003), not stress, so the lead's suggestion to search 3–5 mm thick and 20–40 mm wide points the wrong way. I ran 5 checks, not the ~10 requested, because the result follows from the beam formula:

- Deflection requires E·I ≥ 450 N·m², so b·h³ ≥ 47,450 mm⁴ at nominal load.
- REQ-004 ca

The lightest passing Steel 4130 design is **69 mm wide × 8 mm thick, about 650 g**. The lead's suggested 3–6 mm thickness range doesn't work here: deflection, not stress, is the binding constraint, and it needs the full 8 mm plate.
